title: test-0089-SOC-GEO-DOMAINS
passage: Today in our geography lab, we explored the four major domains of the Earth. We started by looking at a globe to identify the seven continents, which are massive landmasses firmly rooted in the Earth's crust, not floating islands. Next, we examined water samples from different seas and oceans. We discovered that salinity varies significantly depending on the location and evaporation rates, proving that ocean water is not uniform in its salt content. We then turned our attention to the air we breathe. Using a chart, we analyzed the composition of the atmosphere. Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of the air, while oxygen is only 21 percent, showing that nitrogen is actually the most abundant gas. Finally, we discussed the biosphere, which is the narrow zone where land, water, and air interact. We learned that life is not limited to the land surface; it thrives deep within the oceans and high up in the atmosphere, forming a complex web of living organisms across all three domains. This activity helped us understand that the Earth is a dynamic system where these domains constantly support and influence each other in diverse ways.
summary: Today in our geography lab, we explored the four major domains of the Earth. We learned that life is not limited to the land, water, and air — it lives deep in the oceans and high in the atmosphere too!
